md_description: This workflow covers collection of marine microbial seawater samples from diverse oceanic regions, preparation of sequencing libraries, generation of raw sequencing reads, and computational derivation of a dataset suitable for analyzing microbial diversity in relation to latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, biome type, and nearby environmental features such as hydrothermal vents. The final outputs support integrated ecological and genomic analyses across globally distributed marine environments.

marine_seawater_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity and origin/context fields that describe what the marine seawater sample is at collection time: geographic position, collection depth, in situ temperature, biome, and nearby environmental feature context. I excluded downstream process, sequencing, file, and computed-analysis properties because those belong to later Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample/experiment identifier duplication unless needed for this node’s identity, since those are typically generated at the root and should not be repeated if already present elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the collected marine seawater sample (for example, MS-0001). Record once at the entity level to link this sample to downstream concentration, sequencing, and analysis steps.
Latitude of the seawater collection site in decimal degrees at the time of sampling; use WGS84 convention with typical range -90.0 to 90.0, e.g. -33.8651.
Longitude of the seawater collection site in decimal degrees at the time of sampling; use WGS84 convention with typical range -180.0 to 180.0, e.g. 151.2093.

In situ depth below the water surface at which the seawater sample was collected, measured at the sampling site; report in meters, typically 0 to several thousand meters depending on the cruise, e.g. 25.0.
In situ water temperature at the moment and location of sample collection; report in degrees Celsius, typically about -2 to 40 depending on marine environment, e.g. 12.4.
Broad marine biome classification describing the collection environment for the sample at the time of sampling.

Free-text or controlled description of notable nearby environmental features or local context associated with the sampling site, such as proximity to hydrothermal vents, seamounts, reefs, or river plumes; record what was observed or annotated at collection time.

sample_concentration.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing how the seawater sample was filtered or concentrated to produce microbial material for downstream library preparation. I focused on protocol parameters, material/agent details, and a quality indicator for the concentration step. I excluded sample origin fields already owned by the upstream Entity node and any properties of the resulting concentrated material, which belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided repeating identifiers already generated elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Primary method used to enrich microbial material from seawater before library preparation, recorded at the time the process was performed; choose the best matching workflow description for reproducibility.
Nominal pore size of the filter used during concentration, in micrometers, measured as a process parameter when filtration was used; typical values range from 0.02 to 5.0 µm, e.g. 0.22.

Final volume of seawater or retentate processed/retained after concentration, in milliliters, recorded immediately after the concentration step; typical values vary by sample and instrument setup, e.g. 50.0.
Total elapsed time for the concentration step, in minutes, measured from start of filtration or centrifugation to completion; typical range depends on sample load, e.g. 15 to 240 minutes.
Operator-assessed outcome of the concentration step, recorded after completion to indicate whether sufficient microbial material was recovered for downstream library preparation.

concentrated_microbial_material.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the concentrated microbial material itself, not how it was produced or what downstream library prep was done to it. I focused on identity, physical state, source linkage back to the seawater sample, and storage/handling context that is part of what the material is. I excluded process parameters from sample_concentration and downstream sequencing-library attributes, and I avoided repeating any already_generated sample identifiers or other equivalent fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the concentrated microbial material aliquot or retained biomass fraction (for example, CM-0001), assigned to the prepared material after concentration and before library preparation.

Identifier of the upstream marine seawater sample from which this concentrated microbial material was derived (for example, MS-0001); use this to preserve traceability to the original collected sample.
Physical form of the concentrated preparation at the point it is passed to library preparation, such as pellet, filter_retentate, or resuspended_biomass.

Temperature at which the concentrated microbial material was stored after preparation and before library preparation, in degrees Celsius; typical values include -80, -20, 4, or ambient depending on workflow.

Elapsed time the concentrated material was held in storage or awaiting library preparation, in hours, measured from completion of concentration to the start of library preparation; typical range is minutes to days, e.g. 12.5 hours.
Whether the concentrated microbial material was preserved with a stabilizing treatment or kept fresh at the time it entered downstream processing.

library_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing the library preparation workflow itself: the preparation method, key input material amount, indexing/adaptor strategy, amplification settings, and a process outcome indicator. I excluded properties of the resulting sequencing library because those belong on the downstream Entity node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the Capture node. I also avoided repeating already_generated identifiers and any fields that would semantically duplicate the upstream concentrated material or downstream library entity.

md_schema.descr: Name or versioned description of the library preparation protocol used to convert concentrated microbial material into a sequencing-ready DNA library; record the specific workflow at the time of preparation for reproducibility.

Amount of input DNA or nucleic acid material used for library preparation, in nanograms, measured immediately before the library prep reaction; typical ranges depend on kit and sample quality, e.g. 0.1 to 100 ng.
Indexing and adaptor strategy used during library preparation, recorded as the strategy applied to distinguish samples and enable multiplexed sequencing.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library enrichment, recorded at the end of the amplification step; typical range is 0 to 20 cycles depending on input amount and kit, e.g. 8.
Operator-assessed outcome of the library preparation process, recorded upon completion to indicate whether the prepared library met criteria for sequencing input.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared sequencing library: its identity, library type, insert size, concentration, and fragment size profile at the point it is ready for instrument loading. I excluded library preparation workflow parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded instrument configuration and raw file properties because those belong to the downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated sample identifiers or downstream analysis fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library ready for instrument loading (for example, LIB-0001); assign at the library entity level to connect prep, sequencing, and downstream processing.
General library construction type for the sequencing library at the point of loading, such as amplicon, metagenomic, or shotgun, depending on the assay design used for marine microbial sequencing.
Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library immediately before instrument loading, in nanograms per microliter; typical usable range depends on platform and kit, e.g. 0.1 to 100 ng/µL.
Approximate average insert size of the prepared library fragments at the loading stage, in base pairs; typically measured after prep and before sequencing, e.g. 250 bp.

Summary of the library fragment size distribution at the point of sequencing readiness, captured as a qualitative or instrument-derived assessment of whether the library has the expected size profile.

dna_sequencing.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included the measurement session and instrument configuration for the sequencing run: the sequencer identity, run configuration, read layout, chemistry/flow cell information, and a run quality indicator. I excluded sample and library intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file names, file format, and raw read size/dimensions because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also used the agent requirement to capture hardware manufacturer/model/serial-style information on the operation node while avoiding any already_generated field names or equivalent meanings.

md_schema.descr: Hardware manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the run, recorded at the time of capture; for example, Illumina.
Instrument model used for the sequencing capture session, recorded to identify the specific sequencing platform configuration; for example, NovaSeq 6000.
Serial number or equivalent unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session; record exactly as assigned by the manufacturer or facility asset system.
Configured sequencing run mode for the capture session, describing the read layout and throughput setting used for this sequencing experiment.
Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read in the run, measured as the instrument setting for the capture session; typical values include 50, 100, 150, 250, or 300 bp.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit version used during the capture session, recorded as the instrument chemistry setting for reproducibility.
Flow cell type or lane format used for the sequencing run, recorded as the active capture configuration on the instrument.
High-level quality assessment of the sequencing run recorded after capture completion, summarizing whether the instrument session produced data suitable for downstream processing.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only properties of the raw data artefact itself: file identity/location, format, size, read counts, read length, and technical quality indicators. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded processed/analytical interpretations because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating already_generated fields such as sample or library identifiers, keeping the schema focused on the raw read files as delivered from the sequencer.

md_schema.descr: Storage location or path of the raw sequence read file produced by the sequencing instrument, recorded as the delivered raw data artefact path (for example, a FASTQ.gz location in a run directory or object store).
File format of the raw sequencing reads as stored after capture; record the exact technical format used for the raw data artefact.
Size of the raw read file in bytes, measured for the stored artefact after sequencing completion; useful for transfer validation and archival checks.
Total number of reads contained in the raw sequencing file(s), counted from the raw data artefact after demultiplexing or as delivered by the instrument, depending on file organization.
Observed read length in base pairs for the raw reads, measured from the raw sequence file content; typical values should match the configured sequencing read length, e.g. 150 bp.
Technical quality flag for the raw sequence read file(s), recorded after capture to indicate whether the artefact appears intact and usable for downstream processing.

read_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing the computational read-processing workflow itself: the pipeline/software used, key filtering and demultiplexing parameters, trimming thresholds, and a process outcome indicator. I excluded properties of the input raw reads because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the properties of the processed outputs because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided repeating any already_generated field names or semantically equivalent file-quality fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the bioinformatics pipeline used to demultiplex, filter, and summarize raw reads into analysis-ready outputs; record the exact pipeline used for reproducibility.
Version of the read-processing software or workflow recorded at the time processing was run; include the exact version string, for example 2.1.0 or v1.14.
Minimum Phred quality score threshold used to trim or filter bases/reads during processing; typical values are commonly in the range 10 to 40, e.g. 20.
Minimum retained read length in base pairs after filtering and trimming, applied during the read-processing step; typical values depend on assay design, e.g. 50 or 100 bp.
Overall outcome of the read-processing step, recorded after pipeline completion to indicate whether the raw reads were successfully converted into analysis-ready sequence outputs.

processed_sequence_data.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only properties of the processed data artefact itself: file location, format, size, retained read/feature counts, and a technical quality/status indicator. I excluded the computational parameters used to create it because those belong to the upstream read_processing Process node, and I excluded downstream analytical or table-derivation properties because those belong to later Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided any field names already generated elsewhere, including raw-read equivalents and sample/library identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Storage location or path of the processed sequence data artefact produced after computational preprocessing, for example an analysis-ready FASTA/FASTQ table or intermediate file in a workflow directory or object store.
File format of the processed sequence data artefact after preprocessing; record the exact technical format used to store the cleaned data.
Size of the processed sequence data file in bytes, measured after preprocessing has completed and the artefact has been written to storage.
Number of reads remaining in the processed data after filtering, demultiplexing, and cleanup; measured from the output artefact and used to assess processing yield.
Technical quality assessment of the processed sequence data artefact, recorded after preprocessing to indicate whether the output is suitable for downstream feature-table generation.

feature_table_generation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing the computational transformation from processed sequence data into a feature table: the table-generation method, software/pipeline details, key parameters controlling feature definition, and a process outcome indicator. I excluded properties of the processed input signal because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting table’s intrinsic dimensions and storage properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating already_generated field names or semantically equivalent software-version fields beyond what is needed to characterize this process.

md_schema.descr: Method used to convert processed sequence data into a microbial feature table or abundance matrix, recorded at the time of table generation; use the exact method name applied in this workflow.
Software or pipeline name used for feature table generation, recorded as the computational tool that performed the table-building step; for example, qiime2, dada2, deblur, or mothur.
Version of the software or workflow used to generate the feature table, recorded exactly as run to support reproducibility (for example, 2024.10, 1.18.0, or v2.0).

Sequence similarity threshold used to cluster features when applicable, measured as a proportion or percent during table generation; typical values include 0.97, 0.99, or 100% depending on the method.
Overall outcome of the feature table generation step, recorded after the process completes to indicate whether a usable abundance matrix was produced.

microbial_feature_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result properties of the microbial feature table itself: its identity, matrix dimensions, feature-definition basis, value type, sparsity, and an output quality indicator. I excluded the feature-table generation software and parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded input processed-sequence properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node. I also avoided fields already generated for other nodes, especially any sample identifiers and workflow settings.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed microbial feature table or abundance matrix (for example, FT-0001), assigned to the derivative output used in downstream ecological analysis.

Number of samples represented as rows or columns in the microbial feature table, measured from the computed matrix after generation; typical values reflect the number of sequenced marine seawater samples included in the analysis.
Number of microbial features represented in the table, such as ASVs, OTUs, or equivalent sequence features, measured from the computed matrix after generation.
Basis used to define the rows or columns of the feature table at the derivation stage, indicating whether the matrix is composed of sequence variants, clustered taxa, or other computed features.
Type of numeric values stored in the feature table, recorded from the computed output to indicate whether entries are raw counts, relative abundances, or transformed values.
Fraction of zero entries in the computed feature table, calculated after matrix generation to summarize output sparsity; valid values range from 0.0 to 1.0, e.g. 0.92.
Overall quality assessment of the computed feature table, recorded after derivation to indicate whether the output is complete and suitable for downstream metadata integration.

metadata_integration.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the integration workflow details: which software/workflow performed the merge, the join key or linkage strategy, metadata completeness at the time of integration, and an outcome indicator. I excluded the actual sample metadata fields themselves because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded the resulting unified dataset properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields and kept the schema focused on how the linking was performed rather than the linked content.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, script, or pipeline used to link sample-level metadata to the microbial feature table during the integration step; record the exact tool used for reproducibility.
Version of the integration software or pipeline recorded at the time the metadata-feature merge was performed; include the exact version string as run.
Primary key or identifier used to link metadata records to feature-table rows or columns during integration; for example, sample_id or another exact matching field.

Fraction of required sample-level metadata fields available and successfully merged at the time of integration, measured as a proportion from 0.0 to 1.0; use this to document how complete the linked annotations were.
Overall outcome of the metadata integration step, recorded after the merge is complete to indicate whether the unified analysis dataset was successfully created.

annotated_microbial_dataset.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-output properties of the unified annotated dataset itself: its identity, row/column dimensions, the nature of the combined content, file/storage representation, and a quality indicator. I excluded the metadata integration software and linkage parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded the underlying sample and feature-table fields because those are owned by upstream Entity and Derivative nodes, not this unified output. I also avoided repeating already_generated identifiers or semantically equivalent file-path/format fields from raw or processed signal nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the unified annotated microbial dataset (for example, AD-0001) produced after combining microbial features with geographic and environmental metadata.

Number of samples represented in the unified annotated dataset, measured from the computed output after metadata integration; this should correspond to the rows or sample entities available for downstream analyses.

Number of microbial features retained in the annotated dataset, measured from the computed output after integration with metadata; this typically matches or is a subset of the feature table feature count.

Short description of the combined content represented in the annotated dataset, recorded from the computed output to indicate the inclusion of microbial features plus latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, biome type, and environmental context.
File or object format used to store the unified annotated dataset after computation, for example CSV, TSV, BIOM, parquet, or an analysis-project format.
Overall quality assessment of the unified annotated dataset after creation, indicating whether the integrated output is complete and suitable for diversity and association analyses.

diversity_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the analysis workflow details: the diversity-analysis method, software and version, main statistical scope, and an outcome/quality indicator. I excluded properties of the annotated dataset itself because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the computed results because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating already_generated fields and kept the schema focused on how the analysis was performed rather than what the results were.

md_schema.descr: Primary diversity-analysis method applied to the annotated dataset, recorded at the time of analysis; use the exact method category that best matches the workflow used for microbial diversity assessment.
Software, package, or pipeline used to perform the diversity analysis, recorded as the computational tool that executed the statistical evaluation; for example, R, QIIME2, vegan, or Python.
Version of the software or package used for diversity analysis, recorded exactly as run to support reproducibility; include the full version string when available.

Brief description of the ecological or statistical scope of the analysis, such as whether the model focused on latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, biome type, or environmental feature associations.
Overall outcome of the diversity analysis step, recorded after the statistical workflow completes to indicate whether interpretable results were produced.

diversity_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed result properties of the diversity-analysis output itself: result identity, result type, dimensions/counts, effect-size/statistical summary context, and an overall result quality indicator. I excluded the analysis method and software details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded the annotated dataset properties because those belong upstream as well. I also avoided repeating any already_generated identifiers or file-level raw/processed artefact fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed diversity analysis results object or report (for example, DR-0001), assigned to the derivative output generated by the diversity-analysis step.
Primary type of computed diversity output produced by the analysis, recorded from the derivative artifact to distinguish summary tables, association matrices, ordination outputs, or fitted models.
Number of samples represented in the diversity results object, measured from the computed output after analysis; this should reflect the sample count used in the reported summaries or model.
Number of microbial features or variables represented in the diversity results object, measured from the computed output when the result summarizes feature-level associations or model terms.

Concise textual or coded summary of the main statistical effect or diversity pattern captured by the results, recorded from the computed output for downstream interpretation; for example, strongest association direction or dominant gradient.

Overall quality or interpretability assessment of the computed diversity results, recorded after the analysis output is generated to indicate whether the result set is usable for reporting or further review.
